description:
## Contract risk

Canonical `EmailGetParams` at crate-jmap-mail-client/src/methods/mod.rs:40-64
is `#[derive(Debug, Default, serde::Serialize)]` with
`#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` and `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = ...)]`
on each field. The mail-client `email_get` builder serialises it via a single
call: see the canonical pattern in `email_get`.

calendars-client `CalendarEventGetParams` at
crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/mod.rs:101-114 is
`#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]` — NOT Serialize, no `rename_all`, no
`skip_serializing_if`. Each field is manually destructured and inserted into
the args JSON in crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/event.rs:42-52:

```rust
if let Some(p) = params {
    if let Some(v) = p.expand_recurrences {
        args["expandRecurrences"] = v.into();
    }
    if let Some(v) = p.reduced_participants {
        args["reducedParticipants"] = v.into();
    }
    if let Some(v) = p.fetch_calendars {
        args["fetchCalendars"] = v.into();
    }
}
```

## Why this matters for a caller

It does NOT, directly. The caller sees `CalendarEventGetParams { ... }` and
passes it to `calendar_event_get(...)`. The wire effect is identical between
manual destructuring and `serde_json::to_value`.

The contract risk is to the maintainer: adding a new field requires changing
the struct AND remembering to plumb it through `event.rs:42-52`. Forget the
plumbing and the field silently does nothing — no compile error, no test
failure (the current tests assert positive presence of named keys; a
default-None field that never gets plumbed will just be silently absent on
the wire). The maintenance burden is a tax on every contributor.

Also, the manual destructuring opens the door for camelCase typos: a future
field added as `args["expand_recurrences"]` (snake_case) instead of
`args["expandRecurrences"]` (camelCase) would silently send the wrong wire
shape. With `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` the rename is enforced
type-system-wide.

The canonical mail-client pattern centralises the camelCase + skip-None
contract on the struct definition, removing the manual-plumbing tax. Every
contributor adding a field to `EmailGetParams` just needs the `#[serde]`
attributes; the wire shape follows automatically.

## What goes wrong if this stays

Maintenance defect class: a new field added to `CalendarEventGetParams` will
silently not appear on the wire unless someone remembers to update the
manual plumbing. The plumbing site (event.rs:42-52) is far from the struct
definition (methods/mod.rs:101); the connection is implicit.

This will surface as 'I set `params.new_field = Some(true)` and it didn't
work' debugging in some future caller's session. Solvable by Serialize +
single `to_value` call.

## Fix shape

Add `#[derive(serde::Serialize)]` and `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]`
on `CalendarEventGetParams`, add `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`
on each field, and replace event.rs:42-52 with:

```rust
if let Some(p) = params {
    let p_value = serde_json::to_value(&p).map_err(|e| {
        jmap_base_client::ClientError::InvalidArgument(format!(
            "calendar_event_get: serializing params failed: {e}"
        ))
    })?;
    if let serde_json::Value::Object(map) = p_value {
        for (k, v) in map {
            args[k] = v;
        }
    }
}
```

(Or use `args.as_object_mut().unwrap().extend(map)` if you prefer.)

This is related to the missing `extra` field finding — both require the
struct to be `Serialize`. Address together.

title: CalendarEventGetParams not #[derive(Serialize)]; manual field-by-field plumbing in event.rs:42-52 — diverges from canonical
